title: Introduction to Rotational Motion and Angular Momentum

changes.upstream: A large, dark tornado funnel extends from ominous storm clouds down to the ground, with a single tree silhouetted on the left against the dark horizon.

changes.local: Why do tornadoes spin at all? And why do tornados spin so rapidly? The answer is that air masses that produce tornadoes are themselves rotating, and when the radii of the air masses decrease, their rate of rotation increases. An ice skater increases her spin in an exactly analogous manner as seen in . The skater starts her rotation with outstretched limbs and increases her spin by pulling them in toward her body. The same physics describes the exhilarating spin of a skater and the wrenching force of a tornado.
